subject.title: Orphaned lock files not cleared on gateway restart when PID matches current process

question: Should this remain the focused current-PID restart/recovery lock tracker, or should the remaining live gateway-owned lock behavior be moved to a broader session-lock delivery tracker?
rationale: Source inspection shows the original boot cleanup is partially implemented, but reclaiming a lock owned by the live gateway is a transcript data-integrity policy choice that automation should not decide.

options.title: Keep Focused Tracker
options.body: Keep this issue open for same-PID restart/recovery lock semantics while narrower PRs handle compaction, delivery, and diagnostics subcases.

options.title: Move To Broader Tracker
options.body: Close only after explicitly linking the remaining live current-PID behavior to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/86538 and preserving the field evidence there.

options.title: Declare Boot Cleanup Complete
options.body: Treat the startup untracked-self cleanup as sufficient for this issue and open or select a narrower follow-up for live/recovery same-PID lock leaks.

recommendation.title: Keep Focused Tracker
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for same-PID restart/recovery lock semantics while narrower PRs handle compaction, delivery, and diagnostics subcases.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on the lock cleanup policy and live OpenClaw-owned lock boundary.
